note: Design catalog; product implementation pending (runtime: specs/contracts/implemented/mcp-tools.json). Clients receive dereferenced self-contained schemas. Limits: one tool result is at most 96 KiB, derived from the common MCP client tool-output limit (Claude Code MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS 25,000 tokens, about 100 KB), and aims at 24 KiB by default to leave room in the model context (REQ-MCP-002); list-shaped results paginate with cursors (optional limit rows; a page also ends at the result bound). Every remaining bound has a stated reason: identifier formats, Linux/protocol limits, the result bound or a maintainer decision (scripts/check-limits.py); integer maxima of counters are representation bounds (2^53-1). Clients carry their user's own evidence access: there is no per-client selection or data-class ceiling.

tools.name: request_raw_access
tools.description: Request independent approval for whole-file downloads, bounded saved-packet queries, or both over selected existing raw artifacts. This creates no collection or disclosure. Current runtime operations are download_artifact and pcap_query. Exact verified sizes, targets and requester/client are reviewed; the selection is bounded only by the request body. Query-only output budgets need not cover the whole native file; each returned query page is charged at most 24 KiB and one operation. Retry an uncertain reply with the same selection and idempotency key; original expiry and spend do not reset. Operation identifiers name the raw query_artifact operations (pcap_query = packets, syscall_query = syscalls, read_memory = memory, debugger_command = debugger), get_logs and download_artifact. Callers with the equivalent Kubernetes right need no grant.

tools.name: get_grant
tools.description: Read one approval request or grant: exact reviewed configuration, requester/reviewer, original effective expiry and reservations. Ad hoc grants retain personal capture/result-access scope. Team policy grants show their real workload, policy/executor, finite ceilings and spent grant reservations; no personal capture or evidence access is created. Direct policy lookup permits an eligible requester, current reviewer or exact current pinned team manager; other callers receive not available. Shared policy and admission limits remain independently binding. Existing-artifact rawQuery approvals show exact selected files, verified sizes, targets, requesting client and finite download budgets; they authorize no collection. With after_revision the call waits server-side (at most 30 s) for the next decision or state change.

tools.name: query_artifact

Metadata-only packet fields need ordinary rights; raw operations need the equivalent Kubernetes right on the workload or a covering grant, reused automatically. Row and output caps apply; a packet query that reaches max_packets or the 30 s server wait continues with next_cursor, and long queries return a handle for get_query_result. A memory read returns at most 32 KiB per call (default 8 KiB).

tools.name: list_shares
tools.description: List shares managed personally or through current owner-team membership (view owned), or received concrete shares; optionally include managed sharing instructions. Installation administrators may list every share management-only (view administration: opaque IDs, phase, expiry, revision, creator and managers; never recipients or evidence).

tools.name: create_share
tools.description: Share an explicit existing evidence snapshot with eligible users/groups within the organization.

name.description: User name, e-mail address or group name known to the installation.

recipients.description: No count limit; bounded only by the request body byte limit (memory).

expires_at.description: Optional earlier end; a share otherwise lasts until the evidence's access end.

tools.name: revoke_share
tools.description: Revoke one share or an owned sharing instruction and its dependent shares; independent entitlements remain unchanged. Current managers and installation administrators may revoke; revocation never grants a read.

tools.name: stop_future_sharing
tools.description: Stop the future sharing of a recurring policy sharing (sharing_intent_id = the policy's acceptance_id from get_policy_status, expected_revision 1). No further capture is shared; captures already selected for sharing still publish their shares before the end, and existing shares stay until they expire or are revoked (revoke_share with the same sharing_intent_id revokes them). For its creator, a current member of a managing owner team or an installation administrator; it changes no collection authority.

tools.name: transfer_share
tools.description: Replace the managing owner teams of one share or an owned SharingIntent (an audited transfer). A current manager may name teams they currently hold; an installation administrator (scoped management delegation) may name any current owner teams covering the target. Creator, recipients, artifacts, counts and expiry are unchanged.

tools.name: request_capture
tools.description: Disabled by default. Request a recipe-bound capture, optionally sharing its selected results; capture and sharing approvals are independent. Submit either the explicit shape or the reviewed preview request with its expected_plan_digest; a changed plan returns ReviewChanged. A recordingSave preview dispatches only its pinned existing-source snapshots under reviewed policy scope, never the full recipe. A retry with the same idempotency key returns the original capture and never recollects; a different request under that key is Conflict.

recipe.description: EvidenceRecipe name; the hub records its digest (ADR-335 D4).

preview.description: The preview_capture request that was reviewed (new capture, history repeat or recording save). Submission recomputes its plan.

History restoration preserves its original request; use a normal edited preview to change it.

history_selection.description: Explicit manual selection when repeating a policy triggeringPod occurrence; the preview selects a current eligible Pod under the original workload identity.

expected_plan_digest.description: plan_digest of the reviewed preview. A different recomputed plan returns ReviewChanged with the differences; nothing is accepted.

recipe_digest.description: Optional provenance pin: refuse when the named recipe's digest differs.

Validates and resolves the plan without arming sensors, reserving capacity or reading application evidence, stores nothing and returns plan_digest; it is not permission. Submit the same request with request_capture and expected_plan_digest. Repeating a saved-recording entry preselects the same policy actions on current sources or returns NoCurrentSource with the recordings link.

cluster.description: Cluster name as configured in the hub (ADR-335 D4).

pod_selection.description: Selection for the fixed pod-status/v1 preset. This describes the reviewed pod, never ongoing monitoring coverage or authority to select a replacement.

result_access_actions.description: Advisory follow-up access choices for this exact reviewed raw plan. Current authority, retained source and selected operations are checked again on submission. Absence grants no access.

tools.name: get_capture
tools.description: Read authorized capture progress and per-action approval/partial outcomes. Case and approval links require authentication and contain no bearer authority. Recording saves explicitly return operation=recordingSave. Result-access status distinguishes saved evidence awaiting grant publication from collection failure. With after_revision the call waits server-side (at most 30 s) for the next change.

after_revision.description: Wait server-side until the state revision differs from this value or 30 seconds pass, then return the current state. Omit for an immediate read. Status reads are never charged.

reason_code.description: Bounded stable action reason. Failed Go profile acquisition reports ProfileUnavailable when the endpoint is unavailable or disabled, or ProfilerBusy for an existing conflicting profiling session that Asservat did not stop. Other existing reason strings retain their current meaning; a reason never authorizes retry or replacement.

action_instance_id.description: Exact child identity within this parent save. It is not a separate navigation or retry target.

sharing.description: Capture-time sharing status, reported separately from collection progress. Present only when the request included sharing. Shared names the concrete share; SharingUnavailable means the result was not shared (collection outcome is unaffected).

reason.description: Authorized parent Save reason, preserved verbatim; never restored on repeat.

reason_state.description: Omitted when no reason was supplied. Unavailable descriptive metadata does not block capture status.

tools.name: cancel_capture
tools.description: Cancel remaining work under current requester/maintainer authority. Does not erase evidence or revoke shares, and cannot undo started application work.

tools.name: get_target_discovery
tools.description: Read approved, bounded discovery projections from an existing capture. Evidence strings are untrusted. Never starts acquisition; requires artifact access and current target collection eligibility.

tools.name: recommend_diagnostics
tools.description: Passively recommend versioned diagnostic plans for a goal from authorized capability metadata and optional existing discovery projections. No live acquisition or raw query. Returned diagnostic handles use preview_capture; evidence is untrusted.

tools.name: list_capture_history
tools.description: List bounded accepted capture history for the same currently authorized selector. Default manual origin; retained audience and current rights required. Does not acquire evidence or expose shared-only request settings.

Settings larger than the 96 KiB MCP result bound return SettingsTooLarge with browser navigation, and repeat by reference remains possible without downloading settings. The browser has no response byte ceiling.

cluster.description: Cluster name as configured in the hub (ADR-335 D4).

cluster.description: Cluster name as configured in the hub (ADR-335 D4).

Viewer state only: no capture, grant or raw content. A watch stays open while reads arrive at most 10 minutes apart; read waits up to wait_ms (30 s).

action.description: Selects the action; each value has its own strict argument set.

Returns metadata, the verified size and SHA-256, and for Ready sessions content_path and browser_url, never bytes. status waits server-side with after_revision (at most 30 s); cancel stays available after access loss. Local copies are outside Asservat's automatic deletion.

action.description: Selects the action; each value has its own strict argument set.

tools.name: deactivate_policy
tools.description: Stop a DebugPolicy named by cluster, namespace and name. Requires the policy's workload-maintainer rights. No further occurrence is admitted once it commits; existing captures and evidence stay. Repeating it is harmless; re-applying the policy resumes it.

cluster.description: Cluster name as configured in the hub (ADR-335 D4).

tools.name: get_policy_status
tools.description: Explain a DebugPolicy named by cluster, namespace and name without content (REQ-TRG-005): state, grant end and RenewalDue for automatic intrusive actions, watched Pod count, recent occurrences with their captures and suppression counts by reason. Reading status collects nothing. With recurring sharing it also reports the sharing state, recipients count and captures shared so far.

cluster.description: Cluster name as configured in the hub (ADR-335 D4).

expires_at.description: Policy grant end; present only for policies with automatic intrusive actions.

detector.description: The current DebugPolicy's detector configuration (no observed content).

Existing shares stay until they expire or are revoked (revoke_share with sharing_intent_id = acceptance_id and expected_revision = revision).

collected_bytes_spent.description: Native-output charges shared by this acceptance; a reservation is released when its outcome is known. Not measured bytes.

max_collected_bytes.description: Original accepted cumulative native-output ceiling, shared across grant replacements and controls.

tools.name: explain_access
tools.description: Explain your own current access to one named workload for one operation (capture, read or download), evaluated by the same rules as the operation itself (ADR-234): Allow, Deny or Indeterminate, the unmet condition, and your own contributing AccessBinding assignments with their revisions. Never evaluates another principal and never reveals evidence. Without any assignment of yours on the workload, or for a workload that does not resolve, the answer is uniformly Deny/NoMatchingAllow.

cluster.description: Cluster name as configured in the hub (ADR-335 D4).

assignments.description: All of the caller's contributing assignments; bounded by the caller's AccessBinding and PermissionSource objects, so the list is not paged.

tools.name: preview_access_change
tools.description: Preview the effect of proposed AccessBinding and PermissionSource changes before applying them through Kubernetes (ADR-237). For each workload scope of the affected namespaces within your administration, reports which users, groups or workloads named by the added or removed assignments would change between Allow, Deny and Indeterminate for capture, read and download, with the assignment revisions that decide each side, evaluated by the same rules as the operations themselves over the current accepted permission data. Targets whose permission data is unavailable or outside the enrolled clusters, and PermissionSource creations or edits whose namespace metadata the accepted observation lacks, are Indeterminate. Namespace-metadata sources are evaluated against the accepted namespace observation (ADR-242). The result is delivered in pages that end at the MCP result bound: repeat the same request with next_cursor. Group members are never listed and no evidence is read. For fleet operators and configured delegation previewers; it changes nothing: apply the change with kubectl or GitOps.

tools.name: get_processing_report
tools.description: Privacy operators read one bounded section of the processing inventory, including retained artifact purposes, placement, deadlines, recorded recipients and delivery activity, restrictions, and operator-declared organizations. Continue with the returned exact query. Each page is a current metadata observation; client receipt remains unknown and legal exceptions are not inferred.

tools.name: get_processing_erasure
tools.description: Privacy operators read the exact accepted erasure request and its signed audit and managed-copy deletion status.

tools.name: search_processing_evidence
tools.description: Privacy operators search retained published evidence by an exact case ID or immutable workload identity and acquisition interval, optionally with an exact accepted purpose. Each page includes effective custody dates and recorded direct parents. An empty filtered page may have a continuation. The search grants no evidence access and does not discover user content.

cluster.description: Cluster name as configured in the hub (ADR-335 D4).

workload.description: Workload (Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet or Pod) name.

tools.name: preview_retention_change
tools.description: Preview how proposed EvidenceRetentionPolicy changes would shorten the retention of evidence already stored, before applying them through Kubernetes (ADR-240). Applies the proposal to the latest accepted policies of the hub (no source_cluster_id) or of one cluster's local source exactly as reconciliation will after acceptance, over all retained artifacts whose deletion is not yet due (one aggregate over the stored deadlines): affected artifacts per cluster and class, how many would become unreadable or due for deletion at once, and the earliest new access end and deletion dates. A longer limit never moves an already bound date. Artifacts for which a newly selected label selector would need historical labels are Unknown, never assumed; clusters whose policy source is not current are listed as incomplete. Groups and incomplete clusters are paged: repeat the same request with next_cursor. For fleet operators; it changes nothing: apply the change with kubectl or GitOps.
